facts.raw_span: A man in his late 60s presented for evaluation of a right iris lesion
Visual acuity was 20/25 OU
The eye was pseudophakic
10 × 9 × 3.5-mm, well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan, peripheral iris nodule between the 3- and 6-o'clock positions
episcleral sentinel vessels and anterior chamber angle involvement
no visible iris seeding or aqueous cells
Ultrasonographic biomicroscopy: Showed ciliary body involvement
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy results: Showed monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes
Few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes were present
Systemic evaluation: Showed no other involvement
Staging: T2N0M0
Image A: Well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris lesion

concepts.why: The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule with episcleral sentinel vessels and anterior chamber angle involvement, along with the ultrasonographic biomicroscopy showing ciliary body involvement and the fine-needle aspiration biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes, supports the diagnosis of primary iris lymphoma.

The presence of a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes on fine-needle aspiration biopsy, along with the staging of T2N0M0, supports the diagnosis of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, which is a common type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that can involve the iris.

The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule with episcleral sentinel vessels and anterior chamber angle involvement, along with the ultrasonographic biomicroscopy showing ciliary body involvement and the fine-needle aspiration biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes, supports the diagnosis of MALT lymphoma, which is a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that can involve the iris.

The presence of a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes on fine-needle aspiration biopsy, along with the presence of few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes, supports the diagnosis of follicular lymphoma, which is a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that can involve the iris.

The presence of a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes on fine-needle aspiration biopsy, along with the presence of few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes, supports the diagnosis of mantle cell lymphoma, which is a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma that can involve the iris.
